title: 2001: A Space Odyssey
cast: Keir Dullea, Gary Lockwood, Douglas Rain
synopsis: One of the great masterpieces of cinema, Stanley Kubrick’s science fiction epic 2001: A Space Odyssey, is a work of extraordinary cinematic vision. It begins in prehistoric times, then leaps forward into the future of 2001,telling of humanity’s capacity for self-destruction. 2001 remains prescient, especially in our era of Artificial Intelligence. Kubrick wanted to take Science Fiction, a genre often seen as ridiculous, and create an interplanetary spectacle as realistic and believable as possible. Sci-fi author Arthur C. Clarke developed the story, about a mysterious monolith that appears on the moon, which has previously visited earth during a critical stage of human evolution. We then follow an expedition to Jupiter through deep space on a covert mission, derailed by the increasingly odd behaviour of HAL, the distinctively voiced AI that controls their spaceship. In addition to the extraordinary special effects photography, production design and the choreography of the ‘Dawn of Man’ sequence (memorably parodied in Barbie!),Kubrick made iconic use of classical music on the soundtrack, including Richard Strauss’s Also sprach Zarathustra as a recurring theme, and Johann Strauss’s The Blue Danube to accompany the elegant movement of space flight. On release in 1968 (eight months before the actual moon-landings),2001 overwhelmed and fascinated audiences. They were often perplexed by the final section of the film, which Kubrick designed to be a purely visual and sonic journey open to interpretation. It is still utterly mind-blowing 58 years later. synopsis: When ten-year-old Arco steals a time-traveling flight suit to see dinosaurs, a miscalculation strands him in a climate-ravaged 2075. Stripped of the gemstone powering his suit, Arco allies with an imaginative girl named Iris to evade tracking siblings and a rigid robotic police force. As a devastating wildfire closes in, their race home becomes a cross-century fight for survival. Evoking the whimsical wonder of Miyazaki, Ugo Bienvenu’s breathtaking animated debut Arco delivers a rich and imaginative odyssey about friendship, the climate crisis, and the enduring bonds that connect us. If you’ve spent any time on the weirder corners of the internet, you’ve probably heard of the "liminal space" Backrooms phenomenon. For the film adaptation, A24 handed the keys to 20 year old YouTube prodigy Kane Parsons, and he delivered an indie hit that is currently leveling the US box office with a genre piece that skips cheap gimmicks in favor of high art psychological horror. Struggling furniture store owner Clark discovers a bizarre, glowing doorway in his basement that leads directly into the Backrooms—a seemingly infinite, yellow-walled maze that defies all laws of physics. When Clark vanishes into this reality-bending labyrinth, his therapist, Mary, goes in looking for him, only to get trapped in the exact same surreal, mind-warping nightmare. synopsis: In Battambang, Cambodia, a once-beloved cinema stands on the brink of demolition. Sneaking in to document its final days, a journalist named Hai encounters Thida, the spectral guardian of the decaying theater. Faced with the building's destruction, Thida is granted a rare choice: to fade away, or to be reborn into the human world. As the two embark on a metaphysical journey through a rapidly modernizing nation, they find themselves bound by a shared history of displacement. Polen Ly’s debut feature Becoming Human is a gorgeous, meditative film that quietly explores time, memory and resilience, asking how we find a way forward when the places that hold our history and identity disappear. synopsis: TEDxSingapore and Filmhouse present a screening of Dear You in Teochew, featuring a live conversation with Opera Tang and Ah Ma. Who are you still waiting to hear back from? Legacy is usually something we sort out afterwards. We go through the drawers, trying to piece together what they meant, and carry forward a version we are guessing. Together with Filmhouse, we are inviting you, our community to book two seats. Bring your Ah Ma, your Ah Gong, your mother, whoever you have been meaning to ask something. Come join Opera Tang and her Ah Ma, and have that conversation in the present tense. --- Xiaowei travels to Thailand to find his "billionaire grandfather" who is out of contact due to debt problems, but unexpectedly find the one who has been corresponding with his grandmother for years is not her husband. title: Disruption
cast: Dorina Yee, Stephanie Esther Fan
synopsis: DISRUPTION is a psychological thriller created with and alongside disabled filmmakers and performers. Rather than portraying disability as something to overcome, the film challenges society's obsession with "fixing" disability, asking audiences who truly benefits from the idea of being "normal." Developed through workshops with people with disabilities in Singapore, the film combines authentic lived experience with suspense, cinematic storytelling and social commentary. DISRUPTION will be screened with two other films: ASHES & SIGHS, and TEMPLE CRIMES. “DISRUPTION is not a film about disability—it is a film about prejudice. Working alongside disabled writers and performers fundamentally shaped every stage of the production. Their lived experience became the foundation of the story, resulting in a thriller that questions society's obsession with perfection rather than disability itself. If audiences leave questioning those who profit from fear, vulnerability and the promise of impossible cures, then the film has achieved its purpose.” – Ian Dixon

title: Doc Edge Singapore Masterclass: FESTIVALS & BEYOND
Doc Edge Singapore Prelude: A QUIET LOVE
Dollar Trilogy: A FISTFUL OF DOLLARS
cast: Clint Eastwood, Gian Maria Volonté, Marianne Koch
synopsis: “Get three coffins ready.” A mysterious stranger enters a desolate town torn between warring families and plays one side off against the other with deadly consequences. Taking the story from Akira Kurosawa’s Samurai classic Yojimbo, Sergio Leone, infused the most American of genres with a distinctively flamboyant Italian style, creating the ‘Spaghetti Western’. Clint Eastwood – then a TV actor from Rawhide – plays the laconic anti-hero (later known as ‘The Man With No Name’), who cares only for survival and fortune. This was a shocking contrast with moralistic Western ‘good guys’, and Eastwood’s detached cool set the template for the modern action hero. Ennio Morricone’s theme – mixing whistling, church bells, a male choir, and surf guitar, along with orchestra, was a humorous counterpoint to the on-screen mayhem, and paved the way for greater themes to come. Note: All films are in English language without subtitles.

title: Dollar Trilogy: FOR A FEW DOLLARS MORE
cast: Clint Eastwood, Lee Van Cleef, Gian Maria Volonté, Klaus Kinski
synopsis: “This train'll stop at Tucumcari.” The success of Fistful lead to a sequel, and Leone seized the chance to create a more ambitious film. After the startling opening sequence we’re plunged into the cruel, corrupt world of the Old West, where loners track down wanted criminals for money. Eastwood’s cynical bounty hunter crosses paths with sharp-shooter Colonel Mortimer (Lee Van Cleef – a hawk-faced Western regular) who enmeshes him in a plot to find and kill psychopathic bandit El Indio (Italian actor Gian Maria Volonté as one of the great villains) by infiltrating his murderous gang. The Man With No Name wants the reward money, but Mortimer is driven by revenge. For A Few Dollars More unfolds on a larger canvas than Fistful, and Leone’s visual signatures – extreme close-ups against vast landscapes and elaborately violent set-pieces, shift to another level. Morricone’s score is – of course – magnificent. Note: All films are in English language without subtitles. Content Warning: While all three films are rated PG in Singapore, they contain frequent violent scenes. Sexual violence is depicted in FOR A FEW DOLLARS MORE.

title: Dollar Trilogy: THE GOOD, THE BAD AND THE UGLY
cast: Clint Eastwood, Eli Wallach, Lee Van Cleef
synopsis: “Such ingratitude, after all the times I've saved your life.” The third and final ‘Dollars’ film is grander in scale than its predecessor (and any other Spaghetti Western) and arguably Sergio Leone’s finest achievement. The bounty-hunting and treasure-hunting plot revolves around amoral Blondie (Eastwood – reprising this character for the last time), his fractious partnership with chaotic Mexican bandit Tuco (Eli Wallach), pitted against stone-cold killer Angel Eyes (Van Cleef again – as the villain), in a race to claim a secret stash of confederate gold. The saga unfolds against the backdrop of the American Civil War, allowing Leone to mount large-scale, explosive sequences amidst stunning landscapes, while building toward a nerve-shredding three-way duel at a graveyard. As the story twists and turns (with plenty of macabre humour), Leone relishes the scope to tell an epic tale of characters driven by greed and evil. By the finale, they have elevated into the realm of myth and archetype. Morricone concludes the trilogy with some of his greatest music – the main title theme, with its infectious ‘coyote’ cry is his best-known, and the soaring, elegiac The Ecstasy of Gold is extraordinary. Note: All films are in English language without subtitles.

title: Everybody to Kenmure Street
cast: Emma Thompson, Kate Dickie, Keira Lucchesi
synopsis: In May 2021, a UK Home Office dawn raid triggers one of the most spontaneous and successful acts of civil resistance in recent memory. In Pollokshields, Scotland’s most diverse neighbourhood, hundreds of residents rush to the streets to stop the deportation of their neighbours. Programmer's Note: The now iconic sight of an immobilised police van, hemmed in by a sea of commoners, even as more officers arrive, becomes emblematic of the struggle for human rights in an unforgiving world of unjust and discriminatory immigration laws. EVERYBODY TO KENMURE STREET is that galvanising, grassroots work that makes us grateful to know that there are human beings in this world who are compassionate, possess moral courage, and are fearless in their actions. As the film unfolds with gripping immediacy, it also includes generous amounts of archival material of Scottish civil resistance to contextualise the events of Kenmure Street. This is one of 2026's finest documentaries. [Eternality Tan, Vice Chair & Programming Director]

title: Films in Conjunction with Into the Modern
Finding Mojo (Mojoku Hilang!)
cast: Adipati Dolken, Mimi Lana, Wan Hanafi Su
synopsis: At Moo Magic Dairy, Mojo the cow is more than just a mascot—she's a viral sensation. But when her theft sparks a clash between the ruthless dairy conglomerate and the last village of independent farmers, one ambitious young executive finds himself torn between corporate loyalty and rediscovering his roots. Adi, once a village boy, traded his family's dairy farm for a shot at success in the big city. Now tasked with going undercover to recover Mojo and persuade the farmers of Kampung Semerah Padi to sell, he's pulled back into the world he abandoned. There, he reconnects with the land, the people—and with Ayu, а spirited young farmer fighting to save her family's heritage. As secrets of Adi's past unravel, he must choose between the empire he helped build and the community that has come to believe in him. A heartfelt story of family, sacrifice, and belonging, this film explores how the sweetest dreams are rooted in the soil we call home.

title: Girls Like Girls
cast: Maya da Costa, Myra Molloy, Levon Hawke
synopsis: The film title rings a bell? You're probably thinking of that 2015 anthem with the iconic music video that became a touchstone for a generation of queer women. Ten years on, Hayley Kiyoko, affectionately dubbed the "Lesbian Jesus" by fans, brings her beloved song to the big screen in her feature directorial debut! Set over one unforgettable, sun-soaked summer, Girls Like Girls follows Coley, the new girl in town, as she experiences the exhilaration, uncertainty, and vulnerability of first love while learning to embrace who she truly is. Starring Maya da Costa, Myra Molloy, and Zach Braff, the film is a heartfelt coming-of-age story about self-discovery, friendship, and the courage to choose yourself. To celebrate the film's Singapore exclusive release at Filmhouse, we're so excited to present a virtual Q&A with Hayley Kiyoko herself after the Fri 7 Aug, 8.30pm premiere , moderated by local artist and beloved queer icon Jean Seizure. Join us for an intimate conversation about bringing an internet-era cultural phenomenon to the screen, queer storytelling, and Kiyoko's journey from musician to filmmaker. In English Rated R21 for Homosexual Content.

title: HKFGP: Someone Like Me 像我这样的爱情
Hong Kong Film Gala Presentation Singapore 2025
How Can This Be Allow?!
synopsis: A curated selection of Singapore Shorts by Objectifs Centre for Photography and Film. Scratch the surface of the clean and green, and something else stirs. How Can This Be Allow?! reveals a Singapore that doesn't make it into the tourism brochure: desire, repression, and the people who slip through the cracks of a spotless national image. A collision of shorts that shows an alternative side to what we call home. This programme is rated M18 . Presented in collaboration with Objectifs How Can This Be Allow?! will feature the following short films: To Kill The Birds and the Bees by Dir. Calleen Koh 11 min | 2021 | M18 To Kill the Birds & the Bees follows three separate stories of four average Singaporeans – a pair of young twins, a secondary school prefect and a conservative housewife – who each encounter a sexual situation in the course of their day. Someday My Prince Will Come by Dir. Ezzam Rahman 5 min | 2011 | PG Someday my Prince will come – is an experimental video art made in 2011. “Good things come to those who wait” – it is about what lies around the corner, the anticipation of it all, the waiting for something to happen. This video artwork is a depiction of what revolves around themes of yearning, longing, and quiet hope. Ezzam turns his lens towards the complexities of queer desire, particularly the often-isolating journey of seeking connection and companionship. A poignant symbol of vulnerability and tenderness, set against the backdrop of a world increasingly shaped by the unattainable ideals of social-media perfect bodies, flawless skin, curated lifestyles. This video artwork is both a quiet confession and a gentle resistance: a soft, lingering echo of desire in an image-saturated age. Gourmet Baby by Dir. Sandi Tan 15 min | 2001 | PG An idiosyncratic inter-generational relationship plays out across the dining table. A lonely, middle-aged bachelor finds in his niece the perfect dining companion and indulges her in fine dining experiences designed to refine her tastes. However, no amount of fine dining can stop his protégé’s exertion of individuality. Gunkworld by Dir. Mark Chee 10 min | 2020 | NC16 Gunkman, Sallysweets and Roboji are a gang of alien-monster students who terrorise their class with horrifying antics. As Gunkman’s mind-controlling powers escalate beyond the confines of the classroom, no one in the world is safe! I Can’t Sleep Tonight by Dir. K.Rajagopal 9 min | 1995 | PG13 I can't sleep tonight is a tale of three illegal foreigners who meet in Little India one night together unexpectedly not realizing how much they have in common sighnight by Dir. Jake Low 12 min | 2024 | M18 A family that appears ordinary on the surface grapples with the weight of expectations, secrets, and the haunting echoes of cultural traditions during a reunion dinner. "sighnight" is an exploration of the lengths to which individuals will go to preserve familial honour. It is a story of survival, control, and the bonds that tether us to our roots, even as we strive to break free.

title: Itam: A Sun Bear Story
synopsis: Three years in the making, this remarkable documentary was filmed entirely in Sabah, Malaysia. It follows the rehabilitation and release of a rescued sun bear named Itam. Developed in close collaboration with the Bornean Sun Bear Conservation Centre, the production was granted rare access to archival records, veterinary logs, field operations, and the complete rewilding process. This access allows the film to move beyond surface observation into deeply-researched, character-driven storytelling. Combining immersive cinematic language with investigative scientific inquiry, ITAM: A SUN BEAR STORY positions Southeast Asian conservation stories within global discourse. His interest in cross-cultural identity and social issues shaped engineer-turned-filmmaker Raymond Tan’s previous award-winning features, WAYANG BOY and THE WAYANG KIDS, which respectively won Best Foreign Comedy Feature and Best Feature awards in the USA and Chile. “This film is personal because it asks how we measure worth. In a world that often values scale and speed, Itam asks us to slow down and see the dignity of one life. If we can care this much for one bear, the compassion may not be that small after all.” – Director Raymond Tan

title: JACK NEO AWARD GALA: AH BOY To 梁导
King Of Hawkers
cast: Dawn Ho, Ryan Lian, Hugo Ng, Liu Lingling
synopsis: KING OF HAWKERS is a heartwarming Singapore feature film directed by Kelvin Sng that celebrates Singapore's UNESCO-recognised hawker culture through a touching story about family, resilience, heritage and community. First released in Singapore and Malaysia in February 2024, the film follows a woman who returns to Singapore to protect her family's hawker legacy from corporate forces threatening traditional hawker culture. KING OF HAWKERS centres around Zhang Nala (Dawn), who returns to Singapore from Hong Kong to restart her life at her family-run bak chor mee stall after divorcing her rich playboy husband (Collin Chee). Operating next to Nala's stall are others selling local cuisines, such as Ah Lau's Cantonese Cuisine, run by Liu Derong (Hugo) and Bestest Indian Food, which is operated by Raja (Das DD). When a multinational company organises a competition in an attempt to buy over Nala and other hawkers' recipes and businesses, they work together to retain their legacy.

title: Kopitiam Days
director: Yeo Siew Hua, Shoki Lin, M. Raihan Halim, Tan Siyou, Don Aravind, Ong Kuo Sin
cast: Richie Koh, Hong Hui Fang, Zaliha Hamid, Iris Li, Stephen Zechariah, Yang Shi Bin
language: Mandarin, Tamil, Malay, English, Hainanese, Hokkien, Cantonese
synopsis: Commemorating Singapore's 60th year of independence, Kopitiam Days is a stirring anthology film that weaves together six interconnected stories of human connection, reconciliation, and the enduring spirit of Singapore. More than just a setting, the humble kopitiam becomes a living symbol of community and memory, reflecting our past, anchoring our present, and looking towards our future. KOPITIAM DAYS is an anthology of six heartfelt stories that speak of mending relationships and reconnecting, while celebrating Singapore as a home to diverse narratives. We present tales spanning different time periods, with our Kopitiam and the stories it hosts representing the past, present, and future. This anthology will coalesce due to the uplifting nature of the stories, distinctly Singaporean tales that a wide audience can relate to. Each film's ending either signals a new beginning or a newfound appreciation of home.

cast: Chet Baker, Carol Baker, Vera Baker
synopsis: Director Bruce Weber stitches together the life of charming jazz musician Chet Baker through archival footage, interviews, and his time filming with Chet himself a year before his death. Tracing Baker’s early days as a charismatic young trumpeter, his post-accident comeback, and a series of turbulent relationships, this Oscar-nominated documentary is at once a tender act of remembering and a deconstruction of the romanticised myth of Chet. Ratings NC16 for Some Nudity and Drug References.

synopsis: Chiang Hao is a boy who loves the trumpet. To pursue his music dream, he joins the school marching band without informing his father. However, the marching band, which plays outdated martial music, is about to be disbanded. Chiang and his teammates gradually learn to understand each other through many conflicts. They seek to unite, reform the marching band, and encourage each other to strive forward to win the competition. SFS is pleased to present a limited number of public screenings of this remarkable film, which attracted enthusiastic audience response during our recent Singapore Chinese Film Festival. For those who don’t yet know, we urge you to discover for yourselves what the unique connection is, between MARCHING BOYS and THE FELLOW WHO REJECTED COLLEGE!

Her search for its origin leads her through a sound studio, a tunnel, and a stranger who seems to carry the memories of everyone before him. title: Memories of Origin: Hiroshi Sugimoto
cast: Hiroshi Sugimoto, Tadao Ando, Lee U-Fan
synopsis: This documentary follows 200 days in the life of contemporary artist Hiroshi Sugimoto— a leading presence in the world of modern art. He is the winner of many prestigious awards and his photographs are sold for millions of yen at overseas auctions. The film shows the sites of the Architecture series shot in southern France, the huge installation art work at 17th Biennale of Sydney, his new work Mathematics at Provence, his art studio while working on Lightning Fields, and more. It thoroughly pursues the question Sugimoto's works pose - "living in modern times, what are these works trying to tell us?" A thrilling look into the world of Hiroshi Sugimoto. Presenting CINEMATIC VOIDS : a curated film series in collaboration with Singapore Art Museum , accompanying the ongoing exhibition ‘ Hiroshi Sugimoto: Form Is Emptiness’ In Japanese with English subtitles. Rated PG.

title: Mother Bhumi
cast: Fan Bingbing, Natalie Hsu, Bai Run-yin, Pearlly Chua
synopsis: In late-1990s Malaysia, Hong Im, a widowed farmer and ritual healer, struggles to protect her family in a multi-ethnic rice-farming village. By day, she resists land seizures; by night, she heals and exorcises. As colonial-era conflicts resurface, strange events unfold – spirits return, black magic stirs, and a monk leads a buffalo. The legacy of empire haunts the land, the living, and the dead of Bujang Valley. One of the swiftly sold-out films from our Singapore Chinese Film Festival 2026.

title: NIGHT KING 夜王 (with Director Q&A)
Nouvelle Vague
cast: Guillaume Marbeck, Zoey Deutch, Aubry Dullin
synopsis: After writing for Cahiers du cinéma, a young Jean-Luc Godard decides making films is the best film criticism. He convinces producer Georges de Beauregard to fund a low-budget feature, and creates a treatment with fellow New Wave filmmaker François Truffaut about a gangster couple. The result? Breathless , one of the first features of the Nouvelle Vague era of French cinema. Programmer's Note: Linklater reminds us what a remarkable filmmaker he remains, bringing the "hangout" vibe of Dazed and Confused (1993) to the French New Wave era, and, like an obsessive fan, name-dropping the who’s who of that most fertile and discursive period of film history. Playing out like a breezy comedy, as Godard attempts to (valiantly) direct Breathless (1960), his iconic first feature, Linklater portrays the self-appointed cinematic genius with a sense of self-deprecating humour that probably eluded the rebel director. Don't miss this intoxicating love letter to cinema and cinephiles. (Eternality Tan, SFS Vice-Chair & Programming Director)

title: Obsession
cast: Michael Johnston, Inde Navarrette, Cooper Tomlinson
synopsis: Every now and then, a genre film arrives out of nowhere to completely rewrite the theatrical rulebook, and this year, that lightning strike is Curry Barker’s Obsession. The story kicks off when hopeless romantic Bear uses a eerie "One Wish Willow" to make his long time crush, Nikki, fall for him. It works, but with a massive catch: her newfound "love" instantly mutates into a blood soaked, obsessive situationship. Produced on a shoestring budget of under a million dollars, this relentless piece of supernatural terror has exploded into an absolute box office success in the US. At the center of the madness is breakout star Inde Navarrette, delivering an incredibly unhinged and nuanced performance, cleverly using the horror framework to look at deeper anxieties surrounding control, consent, and women's bodily autonomy. Judging by the squirming and collective nervous laughter from our team during our preview screening, you are going to want to witness this instant cult classic in a packed theater full of gasping, screaming filmhomies. In English. Rated M18 for Violence and Sexual Scene.

title: Oldboy - 4K Restoration
cast: Choi Min-sik, Yoo Ji-tae, Kang Hye-jung
synopsis: Long before Parasite and Squid Game hijacked global pop culture, Park Chan-wook’s operatic, Cannes-winning masterpiece completely redefined what a thriller could be. Don't miss out this re-release of the 4k restoration, for a limited time only! Oh Dae-su is abruptly kidnapped off the street and locked in a windowless hotel room for 15 years with no explanation. Just as suddenly, he is released, given a suit, a cell phone, and exactly five days to figure out who ruined his life and why. What follows is a pitch-black, hyper violent journey to the absolute brink of psychological vengeance. In Korean with English subtitles. Rated R21 for Mature Themes. TW: Contains themes of Sexual Violence.

title: On Body and Soul
cast: Alexandra Borbély, Morcsányi Géza, Réka Tenki
synopsis: Before diving into Ildikó Enyedi’s latest work, Silent Friend , revisit the Hungarian master’s Berlinale Golden Bear winning masterpiece that captivated audiences worldwide. Set against the backdrop of a stark Budapest slaughterhouse, two socially awkward co-workers discover they’ve been sharing the exact same dream every night, where they transform into two deer quietly falling in love in a snowy forest. Bizarre, tender, darkly funny, and poetic, On Body and Soul is one of the most uniquely arresting love stories modern European cinema has ever produced. Don't miss this rare big screen pairing! In Hungarian with English subtitles. Rated M18 for Sexual Scenes

title: Painting with Light: Festival of International Films on Art
Palestine 36
cast: Karim Daoud Anaya, Hiam Abbass, Robert Aramayo, Jeremy Irons
synopsis: Year 1936. As villages across Palestine rise against British colonial rule, Yusuf drifts between his rural home and the restless energy of Jerusalem, longing for a future beyond the growing unrest. But history is relentless. With rising numbers of Jewish immigrants escaping antisemitism in Europe and some arriving with nefarious Zionist-colonial ambitions, and the Palestinian population uniting in the largest and longest uprising against Britain’s 30-year dominion, all sides spiral towards inevitable collision in a decisive moment for the British Empire and the future of the entire region. Programmer's Note: Having first met Annemarie Jacir while programming her earlier film, WAJIB (2017), I recall her reflection that Palestinians often live lives preordained by external forces. PALESTINE 36 arrives as a timely work set against the 1936–39 Arab Revolt, foregrounding the British Empire’s role in shaping the conditions of political oppression and violence in Palestine. Incorporating documentary footage alongside measured melodrama, Jacir builds a film that is both accessible and resonant, where its power lies in drawing empathetic parallels with the present moment, inviting us to rethink moral and historical justice. (Eternality Tan, Vice-Chair & Programming Director)

title: Raya & the Last Dragon
synopsis: Long ago, in the fantasy world of Kumandra, humans and dragons lived together in harmony. But when an evil force threatened the land, the dragons sacrificed themselves to save humanity. Now, 500 years later, that same evil has returned and it's up to a lone warrior, Raya, to track down the legendary last dragon to restore the fractured land and its divided people. However, along her journey, she'll learn that it'll take more than a dragon to save the world- it's going to take trust and teamwork as well. title: Rubbers
cast: Marcus Chin, Yeo Yann Yann, Alaric Tay, Oon Shu An, Catherine Sng
synopsis: The stories of three people looking for love and physical connection are interwoven in playfully raunchy tales revolving around condoms. Singapore’s first R21-rated sex comedy has three non-intersecting storylines – realism (Balloons), magical realism (Plumber), and absurdist (Nightmare) – revolving around condoms, in the contexts of saving a failing marriage, seducing a plumber, and punishing a selfish playboy. With a veteran local cast including Golden Horse award-winner Yeo Yann Yann, RUBBERS has earned an indelible place in the history and output of Singapore filmmaking. Look out for a note-perfect ‘Asian horror’ sequence starring the director himself.

title: SGIFF: THIS CITY IS A BATTLE FIELD
Silent Friend
cast: Tony Leung Chiu-wai, Léa Seydoux, Luna Wedler
synopsis: On the grounds of a medieval German university town looms an imposing Ginkgo biloba, a tree whose longevity stands in marked contrast to three intimate, human-scaled stories. In 1908, the university’s first female student gains admission into the prestigious botany department, confronting the sexism of both professors and peers. In 1972, amidst counterculture movements, a reserved student finds his attention captured by a fellow housemate and the geranium plant she studies. In 2020, during the COVID-19 pandemic, a neuroscientist from Hong Kong secures the help of a renowned botanist for an experiment on the old ginkgo tree. In German, Cantonese and English with English subitles. Rated M18 for Some Nudity and Drug Use.

synopsis: Please Note this screening has SOLD OUT. To mark the 20th anniversary of the critically acclaimed film Singapore Dreaming (2006), directed by Woo Yen Yen and Colin Goh, and executive produced by Dr Woffles Wu, the Asian Film Archive presents two special screenings in August, accompanied by post-screening Q&A sessions with the filmmakers and cast […]

title: Singapore Minstrel (10th Anniversary)
synopsis: A fantasy-documentary painting the magical universe of Singapore’s wildest busker Roy Payamal is the wildest busker of a country ranked the world’s most emotionless society. He takes his undermined line of work as a serious art- but is his faith impossible idealism or an admirable conviction? Singapore Minstrel is an invitation into his beautiful mind, a magical, trying universe where art and life dialogue in a tropical dream. In English with English subtitles. Rated PG. Join us for a live Q&A with director Salty Xi Jie Ng and artist Roy Payamal, moderated by Viknesh Kobinathan on Sat 8 Aug 2pm. Salty Xi Jie Ng is an artist, performer, educator, and mystic based between Singapore and Portland, Oregon. Her transdisciplinary practice is a collaborative, alchemical site intimately exploring the erotic, ancestry, ageing, the inner worlds of older women, the end-of-life, unseen worlds, and spirit realms, while examining artistic labour and what gets to be called art. Salty is the 2024 recipient of the Chamberlain Award for social practice artists from the Headlands Centre for the Arts and the 2025 Arts Research Scholar-in-Residence at Nanyang Academy of Fine Art - University of the Arts Singapore. Viknesh Kobinathan is a cultural worker and organiser whose practice explores gatherings around sound and image as acts of care, healing, rest, and refusal. He holds a postgraduate degree in Film Studies from the National Film and Television School in England. Based in Singapore, he is part of the film programming team at Objectifs – Centre for Photography and Film. He was previously Programmer at the Asian Film Archive and Programme Manager at The Projector.

cast: Rumi Hiiragi, Miyu Irino, Mari Natsuki
synopsis: A young girl, Chihiro, becomes trapped in a strange new world of spirits. When her parents undergo a mysterious transformation, she must call upon the courage she never knew she had to free her family. In Japanese with English subtitles, Malay and Chinese subtitles. Rated PG.

title: Stalker
cast: Alisa Freyndlikh, Aleksandr Kaydanovskiy, Anatoliy Solonitsyn
synopsis: A faithful stalker guides a melancholic writer and a skeptical scientist into the Zone, a stretch of heavily guarded land where the ordinary laws of physics no longer apply. At its centre lies a room said to grant a person's deepest, innermost desires. Tarkovsky's most well known masterpiece, Stalker, turns the spectacle of the Zone into an introspection for the three men inside it. In this liminal nothingness, the camera lingers on moss and rust and water until stillness feels comfortable. cast: Homayoun Ershadi, Abdolrahman Bagheri, Safar Ali Moradi
synopsis: A man drives around Tehran searching for someone to bury him after he takes his own life. Along the way, he meets strangers who each try, in their own way, to talk him out of it. Taste of Cherry, Abbas Kiarostami’s most recognised work, won't let you down with the simple yet profound journey it takes you on. title: Temple Crimes
cast: Tristan Pu Pang Kit, Mark Seow Wei Yuen
synopsis: Venturing into an overgrown graveyard, eleven-year-old Chinese boy, Bojing, transforms his fear of strangers into belief in the maturity of Ken, an escapee from Singapore’s maximum-security prison, Changi. But, having smuggled Ken to a nearby stone temple, Bojing soon discovers the truly criminal mind of his new dark mentor. Ultimately, however, it is the eleven-year-old Bojing who proves the greater hero and mentor... TEMPLE CRIMES will be screened with two other films: DISRUPTION and ASHES & SIGHS.

title: The Big Picture- Fortnightly Film Screening
synopsis: In this musical comedy classic, two musician brothers discover that their former orphanage is in financial ruin. They decide to raise funds to prevent its closure.

title: The Fellow Who Rejected College
cast: Wang Fu-shih, Peng Hsueh-fen, Chang Pei-hua
synopsis: Deemed as one of the Top 10 Chinese-Language Films of 1980, THE FELLOW WHO REJECTED COLLEGE is adapted from a bestselling novel, which was once praised by renowned writer Sanmao as "Taiwan’s ‘The Catcher in the Rye’." The film tells the story of a group of high- achieving senior high school students striving for academic excellence amidst intense competition, as they prepare for the challenging and highly aspirational university entrance examinations. A top student sends shock waves through his family and friends when he decides not to take them. Singapore Film Society Chairman Kenneth Tan loves this film so much that he has watched it a total of 59 times on the big screen. It is literally the movie that changed Kenneth’s life, instilling in him a deep sense of affiliation and affection for Cinema, and inspiring him to embark on his lifelong career in the industry.

title: The Invite
cast: Seth Rogen, Olivia Wilde, Penélope Cruz, Edward Norton
synopsis: You’re cordially invited to the most chaotic dinner of the year. Fresh from its buzz heavy Sundance debut, Olivia Wilde’s razor sharp relationship comedy hits right where it hurts. Joe (Seth Rogen) and Angela (Wilde) are stuck in a domestic rut, made worse by the aggressively loud, boundary pushing love life of their upstairs neighbors, Hawk (Edward Norton) and Pina (Penélope Cruz). Hoping to smooth things over, Angela invites them down for a casual dinner party. But as the wine flows, polite small talk is instantly traded for a chaotic, hilariously uncomfortable truth game where social etiquette completely crumbles. In English Rated M18 for Mature Content and Coarse Language.

title: The Mysterious Gaze of the Flamingo
cast: Tamara Cortés, Matías Catalán, Paula Dinamarca
synopsis: In the Chilean desert of 1982, eleven-year-old Lidia is raised within a fiercely protective queer household. But when a fatal disease sweeps her village, a dark superstition takes hold: that the illness spreads through a single glance between two men in love. Suddenly targets of intense hostility, Lidia embarks on a quest for truth and vengeance, navigating a volatile landscape of fear where her family is both her sole sanctuary and the ultimate source of her peril. Balancing absurdist wit with deep poignant urgency, The Mysterious Gaze of the Flamingo forces us to confront how easily fear can weaponize love, and the lengths we must go to shield those we cherish. Fireside Chat: Join us on Wednesday 5 August's session for a post-show Fireside Chat with Project X. In Spanish with English subtitles. Rated M18 for Mature Content. title: The Odyssey
cast: Matt Damon, Tom Holland, Anne Hathaway
synopsis: Leave it to Christopher Nolan to take a 3,000-year-old high school reading assignment and turn it into an epic popcorn blockbuster that doubles as a sharp critique of hubris, greed, and the human cost of imperialism. Following the fall of Troy, King Odysseus embarks on a treacherous ten-year journey across the Mediterranean to return to his kingdom of Ithaca. While he navigates terrifying monsters and the wrath of sea gods, his wife Penelope must hold their home together against a ruthless horde of suitors claiming his throne and his family. In English. Rated NC16 for Violence.

synopsis: An aging widower's plan to sell his cherished car before relocating overseas takes an unexpected turn when he meets a transgender potential buyer, leading to new perspectives as his departure date shifts.

title: The Story of Southern Islet
cast: Jojo Goh, Season Chee, Pearlly Chua, Ling Tang
synopsis: A wife finds herself thrown into a complicated world of spiritual confusion when her husband is struck down by a mysterious illness he himself attributes either to black magic or divine wrath. Chong Keat Aun’s feature directorial debut is partly a treatise on the absurdity of national borders but also one of cosmological ambiguity in which the acceptance of that which cannot be explained provides the only hope of a cure for those burdened by the sin of transgressing against the gods. THE STORY OF SOUTHERN ISLET won the Golden Horse Best New Director Award, as well as the FIPRESCI Prize at both the (2020) Golden Horse and (2021) Hong Kong International Film Festivals. “Beautifully shot with a lingering ethereality, Chong’s mystical tale places gods and demons amid the everyday while demonstrating the ebb and flow of deeply held cultural beliefs in a border community where harmonious coexistence has long been the norm.” -- Hayley Scanlon, Windows on Worlds

title: The Towering Inferno
cast: Steve McQueen, Paul Newman, William Holden, Faye Dunaway, Fred Astaire
synopsis: THE TOWERING INFERNO, one in a string of disaster movies of the 1970s, was promoted as a tribute to firefighters and their heroic work. It was also among the highest-grossing box office draws of the mid-1970s. The finishing touches have just been made to the Glass Tower, a 138-story skyscraper in the heart of San Francisco. A huge celebratory gala, complete with VIP invitees, has been planned to celebrate the dedication of what has been promoted as the world's tallest building. But the building's architect, Doug Roberts, suspects all is not right with the construction. The contractors have used shoddy materials, not the heavy-duty wiring he had specified. The overworked system develops short circuits, coincidentally enough during the height of the celebratory extravaganza; it isn't long before the building is ablaze and hundreds of people become trapped on the 135th floor, where the party takes place. Fire Chief Michael O'Hallorhan immediately devises a daring plan to rescue the trapped guests, but his efforts quickly become a battle against time and the panicked guests. A breathtakingly spectacular epic film, even after many decades!

synopsis: January 29, 2024. Red Crescent volunteers receive an emergency call. A five-year old girl is trapped in a car under fire in Gaza, pleading for rescue. While trying to keep her on the line, they do everything they can to get an ambulance to her. Her name was Hind Rajab. In Arabic with English Subtitles. Rated R21 for Mature Content.

title: The World of Love
cast: Seo Su-bin, Jang Hye-jin, Kim Jeong-sik
synopsis: This touching drama tells the story of Jooin, an enigmatic 17-year-old high school student. She is a cheerful friend, a shameless daughter, a mischievous girlfriend, and a person who is always hard to predict. One day, after a fellow classmate asks Jooin to sign a petition to prevent a newly released sex offender from moving into their neighbourhood, Jooin refuses, causing a major scene. She starts to receive anonymous notes questioning her behavior, and cracks begin to appear in her formerly peaceful world. Join us on 2 and 3 July for an in-person Q&A with Director Yoon Ga-Eun. "I even felt professional jealousy." — Bong Joon-ho on THE WORLD OF LOVE In Korean with English subtitles. Rated PG13 for Some Sexual References. title: Trainspotting (4K Restoration)
cast: Ewan McGregor, Ewen Bremner, Jonny Lee Miller
synopsis: Danny Boyle's decade-defining adaptation of Irvine Welsh's Trainspotting celebrates its 30th anniversary in 2026, and is heading back to Filmhouse from 21 August in a 4K restoration as part of our Music In Film showcase! Ewan McGregor stars as Mark Renton, the most reflective member of a group that also includes the compulsive womaniser, Sick Boy (Jonny Lee Miller), and the hapless Spud (Ewen Bremner). Renton, Spud and Sick Boy's issues with drugs alternatively irritate and amuse their friend, Begbie (Robert Carlyle), a periodic psychopath whose outbursts of violence are one of the many factors that convince Renton to leave for London in the hope of starting a new life. Renton enjoys some success remoulding himself as an estate agent in the English capital, but it isn't long before his Edinburgh friends catch up with him. Begbie and co. need the money Renton has saved from his job to finance the drug deal that could make them all rich... In English. Rated R21 for Drug Use and Sexual Scenes

title: Two Seasons, Two Strangers
cast: Shim Eun-kyung, Shinichi Tsutsumi, Yuumi Kawai
synopsis: What begins as a youthful summer romance against deep sea blues is revealed to be a screening of Li's film, a writer paralyzed by creative block. Seeking escape, she retreats to a snowy resort, where a tentative connection with a divorced innkeeper starts to mirror her own fiction. Reminiscent of Hong Sangsoo’s bifurcated storytelling, Two Seasons, Two Strangers (旅と日々) explores art and isolation through contrasting landscapes of sea, snow, and silence. Fresh off its Golden Leopard win at Locarno, this poetic film eloquently captures the limits of language-- letting the environment speak where words fail, and finding a comforting grace in shared loneliness.
